title: Similar figures
summary: Recognise similar figures and work with one constant linear scale factor.
objectives: Use scale factors for sides, perimeters and areas.

blocks.text: Similar figures have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. A scale factor of 1 gives congruent figures; any other positive factor changes size.

Similar figures have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding lengths. The image length equals scale factor times original length. Perimeters use the same linear factor, while areas use the square of that factor.

Choose one direction for the scale factor and keep it throughout. If the factor from A to B is k, then length_B=k×length_A, perimeter_B=k×perimeter_A and area_B=k²×area_A. A scale factor of 1 gives congruent figures.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: A 6 cm side becomes 15 cm in a similar figure. Find the scale factor.

sections.verification_note: Check that every side and angle was matched in the stated corresponding order.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Two similar rectangles have areas 54 cm² and 150 cm². A side of the smaller rectangle is 9 cm. Find the corresponding side of the larger rectangle.

sections.verification_note: The length factor 5/3 squared gives the area factor 25/9.

blocks.text: Do not apply the area factor directly to a length. Keep original and image in the same order in every ratio. Similar figures need equal corresponding angles as well as proportional sides.

prompt.text: A perimeter of 20 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. Find the new perimeter.

blocks.text: Write the correspondence first, use one consistent scale factor, preserve equal angles, and check whether a length, perimeter or area needs a linear or squared factor.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
